thread:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT: Eviction spikes on node gpu-pool-7 -> runtime crash suspected (sev2) :rotating_light:
Alex Kim: hitting a flurry of pod evictions on gpu-pool-7, multiple modelcache pods got EVICTED, then runtimes started failing with CUDA init errors. paging oncall now.
Maria Gonzales: on it, grabbing kube events/logs. which cluster?
Alex Kim: prod-west (k8s-prod-west-1). pattern: ephemeral-storage pressure -> eviction -> modelcache restart -> runtime OOM/CUDA failures.
Samir Patel: any operator messages? I see kubelet eviction logs for /var/lib/modelcache tmp dir.
Jordan Lee: past 5m: node reports disk.available < 1GB then kubelet issues EvictionThresholdReached, pods with local-storage annotation prioritized for eviction.
Isha Rao: which customers hit 5xx? I can triage impact.
Alex Kim: Ambassador routing shows ~15% error rate for a single high-traffic customer and a handful of internal canaries. Not global but degraded.
pagerduty-bot: @oncall_prod_west assigned to Maria Gonzales (page).
Maria Gonzales: quick dump: `kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-pool-7` -> many modelcache-* in CrashLoopBackOff and model-serve-* with Error: "CUDA error: driver not initialized"
Samir Patel: paste of kubelet evict log: ```May  7 14:35:12 kubelet[1]: eviction manager: attempting to reclaim ephemeral-storage```
Maria Gonzales: also saw a bunch of large rotated logs in /var/log/containers - modelcache logs grew massively due to DEBUG enabled during a recent rollout.
Jordan Lee: can we free disk quickly? Options: 1) SSH and rm old logs 2) scale down log verbosity 3) drain node and evict gracefully 4) reconfigure eviction thresholds in patch - risky.
Isha Rao: customers affected: cust-omega (high qps), internal-staging. Cust-omega reporting timeouts on embeddings endpoints. Notifying support now.
Alex Kim: immediate mitigation I propose: 1) cordon gpu-pool-7 2) delete largest rotated logs from /var/log/containers (compress+move) 3) restart kubelet? 4) re-route traffic away by bumping weights in routing policy for prod-west to fallback region.
Samir Patel: agree. I'll take node maintenance: SSH -> move rotated logs to tmpfs on ephemeral/remote and rm originals. prepping commands now.
Maria Gonzales: copying `sudo du -sh /var/log/containers/* | sort -h | tail -n 10` gave ~12GB from two modelcache pods.
Samir Patel: running: ```sudo systemctl stop kubelet && sudo rm -rf /var/log/containers/modelcache-*old.log && sudo systemctl start kubelet``` — will do safe deletes (mv -> gz -> rm).
Jordan Lee: while Samir cleans, I'll flip the routing: shift 30% of prod-west traffic to prod-east canary pool and enable fallback to smaller quantized model variants to reduce mem.
Isha Rao: support update posted to cust-omega: "We've detected intermittent timeouts; engineers are mitigating. We'll update in 15m."
Alex Kim: FYI observed after eviction: some modelcache restarts favored host memory reclaim but the runtime process then failed to mmap VMA leading to CUDA driver init errors. likely corrupted cache metadata after sudden eviction.
Maria Gonzales: after log pruning node free ~18GB. Starting drain: `kubectl drain gpu-pool-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` now.
Samir Patel: drain in progress. Deleting modelcache pods with local-storage annotation, allowing graceful restarts on other nodes with more space.
Jordan Lee: routing changes applied: prod-west weight -30% -> prod-east. Canary run shows error rate normalized to baseline on new hosts.
Isha Rao: customer impact: cust-omega 5xx rate dropped from 15%->2% after traffic shift. Support informed.
Alex Kim: next: we should avoid immediate re-scheduling of heavy modelcache pods to nodes with small ephemeral. Plan: taint nodes with low disk and add pod affinity to prefer nodes with SSD.
Maria Gonzales: agreed. I'll create a temporary node taint: `kubectl taint nodes gpu-pool-7 disk-pressure=true:NoSchedule` to keep scheduler from bouncing back.
Samir Patel: done. also rotating modelcache logs in rolling fashion and disabling DEBUG for the patched rollout (PR #2345).
Jordan Lee: long term ops items: 1) adjust eviction thresholds for ephemeral-storage on gpu pools 2) enable logrotate for container logs (max 200MB) 3) add pre-drain hook to flush modelcache to S3 or persistent cache 4) add healthcheck to detect corrupted cache metadata and fallback to cold load instead of crash.
Isha Rao: creating customer-facing postmortem draft and timeline. ETA 1 hour for initial impact and mitigation notes.
Alex Kim: quick gotcha: some pods failed with `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` after restart — we should restart runtime nodes only after we ensure modelcache metadata is reindexed. I'm running a forced cache-reindex on one instance off-traffic.
Maria Gonzales: cache reindex ran on canary node, success; runtimes on that node came up clean.
Samir Patel: kube drain finished, node cordoned, new pods scheduled to other nodes with available disk.
Jordan Lee: I'll open a PR to set eviction threshold to 1.5Gi for now on gpu pool and add a monitoring alert for /var/lib/modelcache > 70% usage.
Isha Rao: support message updated: "Mitigation in place: affected node removed from rotation; traffic routed to alternate region; engineers are performing cache reindex and JVM restarts. We'll follow up with root cause and next steps."
Alex Kim: final immediate actions checklist: - [x] cordon + taint node - [x] prune logs - [x] drain node - [x] reroute traffic - [x] reindex cache on canary - [x] update support message
Maria Gonzales: paging down oncall, leaving followup tasks assigned: Samir (logrotate + PR), Jordan (eviction threshold PR + alert), Alex (postmortem timeline), Isha (customer comms).
pagerduty-bot: Incident resolved -> mitigation complete, incident escalated to zero outstanding oncall pages.
Alex Kim: we'll keep this thread for postmortem notes. Great work everyone. :clap:
